story.name: ジャスミンの きっさてん
story.title: A Bargain from Redd
story.line: つねきちから あやしい マシンを かいます
story.ja: つねきちの船に「本物のイタリア製、ほとんど新品」のエスプレッソマシンが。安すぎるけれど、ジャスミンは買ってしまう。ところが、悲しいガチョウのような音を出して、蒸気をふきだすばかり。ちゃちゃまるが直そうとしてさらに悪化。そこへマスターが来て、それが昔の自分のマシンだと気づく。

segments.en: A few days later, a small boat with a patched green sail pulled up to the pier.
It belonged to Redd, who sold art, furniture, and other things nobody asked too many questions about.
Well, well. A little bird told me somebody's opening a café. And I just happen to have exactly what you need.
He pulled back a blanket. Underneath was an espresso machine.
It was old, and a little dented, but it was copper and brass, and it gleamed in the sun.
Genuine Italian. Hardly used. Belonged to a famous barista, very hush-hush. For you? Half price. Because I like your face.
Pekoe knew that a deal this good was usually too good to be true. Everyone on the island knew that about Redd.
But it was so beautiful. And it was, for once, almost in her price range.
She looked at it for a long time, and then she counted out her savings.
Okay. I'll take it. But if it doesn't work, I'm coming to find you. I know where your boat is.
Doesn't work? Please. That thing'll outlive both of us. Pleasure doing business with you, sweetheart.
And his little green sail was gone around the point before she had even plugged it in.
She filled it with water. She turned the big brass knob. The machine shivered. It rumbled.
And then it made a long, sad sound, like a goose with a broken heart.
A cloud of steam shot out of the side and fogged up every window in the shop. But no coffee came out. Not a single drop.
Dom heard the noise all the way from the beach and came running, still holding his jump rope.
Whoa, what was that? It sounded like a goose. Is everybody okay in here? Is there a goose?
No goose. Just me, and the most expensive mistake I've ever made in my whole life.
Hey, don't worry about it. I'm pretty handy. Let me take a look. How hard can it be?
It turned out to be very hard. Dom found a wrench and tightened everything in sight.
The machine made the goose noise again, only louder, and then it whistled.
By the afternoon, they were sitting on the floor in a cloud of steam, and the machine seemed to be laughing at them.
That's when the door opened, and Brewster walked in. He did not say hello.
He walked straight to the machine and looked at it for a very long time.
I know this machine. That dent on the side, I made that dent. This was my first machine, a long time ago.
Wait, it was yours? But Redd said it belonged to a famous barista in Italy.
I've never been to Italy. I gave it away when I bought the new one. I'm not sure how it ended up on Redd's boat.
He tapped the side of the machine twice, gently, the way you might wake up a sleeping cat. Then he waited.
It needs a new rubber ring, here, by the handle. And you have to be patient with it. It takes a minute to wake up. Like me.
The next morning, there was a small paper bag on the counter. Inside was a brand new rubber ring and a note that just said, B.
Pekoe put the ring in, tapped the side twice, and waited. The machine hummed.
And then, slowly, a thin stream of dark, perfect coffee came out into her cup.
Oh my gosh. Oh my gosh, it works. Dom! Dom, come here, it actually works!
That evening, Redd's green sail came back around the point. He leaned on the doorframe and smiled his biggest smile.
See? What did I tell you? Genuine Italian. You can't put a price on quality. Well, you can. And you did.
Pekoe didn't argue. She just made him a cup of coffee, on the house. And Redd, for once in his life, didn't have anything to say.

predict.ask: つぎに こまる ことは？
choices: Her menu is so long that nobody can choose.
The machine breaks again on the first day.
Redd opens a café right next door.
predict.ja: メニューが長すぎて、だれも選べない。
